title: Finite-size effects and interaction-driven crossovers in quarter-filled attractive Hubbard model: Exact diagonalization, DMRG and machine-learning analysis
abstract: We investigate the quarter-filled attractive Hubbard model on finite-width cylindrical lattices using exact diagonalization (ED), density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and unsupervised machine-learning-based techniques. Analysis of the ground-state energetics, local observables and correlation functions reveals a continuous interaction-driven crossover from weakly correlated fermions to a regime dominated by tightly bound singlet pairs. This crossover originates from the competition between kinetic-energy-driven fermionic itinerancy and interaction-driven onsite pair formation and exhibits behavior consistent with the BCS--BEC crossover in the thermodynamic limit. Hole-binding-energy calculations provide direct energetic evidence for pair formation: the two-hole binding energy remains negative throughout the attractive regime whereas three-hole binding emerges only at sufficiently strong attraction and exhibits pronounced finite-size dependence. To obtain an unbiased characterization of the correlation landscape, we apply principal component analysis (PCA) and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) to the real-space correlation matrices. PCA reveals a systematic redistribution of correlation variance whereas UMAP identifies a clear separation between weak- and strong-pairing regimes. Both machine-learning-based approaches independently identify the same crossover region inferred from conventional observables while providing an order-parameter-independent characterization of the underlying reorganization of many-body correlations. Finite-size scaling analyses of the pairing structure factor and the leading PCA variance ratio demonstrate that these signatures remain robust with increasing system size.
summary: The authors study the crossover in the attractive Hubbard model, transitioning from itinerant fermions to tightly bound pairs. They combine DMRG and ED calculations with advanced machine learning tools like PCA and UMAP to map this complex correlation landscape. The findings robustly confirm the BCS-BEC crossover analogy while offering a generalizable methodology for characterizing quantum phases.
main_problem: The study investigates finite-size effects and interaction-driven crossovers within the quarter-filled attractive Hubbard model.
main_result: The analysis confirms a continuous crossover from weakly correlated fermions to tightly bound singlet pairs, consistent with the BCS–BEC crossover analogy. Machine learning techniques independently validate this crossover region by characterizing correlation reorganization.
method: A combination of advanced numerical simulations (ED, DMRG) and unsupervised machine learning dimensionality reduction (PCA, UMAP) is employed on real-space correlation matrices.
model_or_system: The system is the quarter-filled attractive Hubbard model defined on finite-width cylindrical lattices. The Hamiltonian involves hopping ($t$) and an attractive onsite interaction ($U$).
key_observables: Ground-state energetics, local observables (e.g., double occupancy), pairing structure factor, and leading PCA variance ratio.
important_parameters: Attractive interaction strength ($U$), finite system size ($L_y 	imes L_x$), and the quarter-filling condition ($n=0.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on extrapolating results from finite clusters to the thermodynamic limit using finite-size scaling techniques.
figures_summary: Tables summarize fitting parameters for the pairing structure factor and the leading PCA variance ratio derived from finite-size scaling analyses, showing systematic changes across the crossover region.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies ED/DMRG to calculate observables across varying interaction strengths. It then uses PCA and UMAP on correlation matrices to map the underlying quantum phase space, confirming results via finite-size scaling analysis of key diagnostics.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, order-parameter-independent diagnostic tool (PCA/UMAP) to characterize complex many-body crossovers in lattice models, which is highly relevant for interpreting experimental data from ultracold atoms simulating Hubbard physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Ground-state energy per site E0/M as a function of U for Ly × 4 cylinders (Ly = 2, 3, 4) at quarter ﬁlling, computed using ED (circle) and DMRG (square). Excellent agreement between ED and DMRG is observed. Inset: Excitation gap ∆E = E1 −E0 obtained from ED. The broad maximum of ∆E at intermediate attraction signals a crossover from weakly bound fermions to strongly paired regime.

FIG. 2. Average double occupancy ¯d as a function of U for quarter-ﬁlled Ly ×4 cylinders (Ly = 2, 3, 4). Inset: average local moment ¯m. Increasing attraction enhances onsite pair forma- tion, resulting in a monotonic increase of ¯d and a corresponding suppression of ¯m.

FIG. 4. Pair-pair correlation function P1j as a function of dis- tance R for (a) 3 × 4 and (b) 4 × 4 cylinders at quarter ﬁlling. Here site 1 is chosen as the reference site. Increasing attrac- tive interaction enhances both the magnitude and spatial extent of pairing correlations, indicating the progressive formation of bound singlet pairs.

FIG. 3. Charge structure factor SD(π, π) as a function of U for quarter-ﬁlled Ly × 4 cylinders (Ly = 2, 3, 4). Inset (a): spin structure factor SL(π, π). Inset (b): singlet pairing structure factor SP (0, 0). Increasing attractive interaction suppresses spin correlations while enhancing charge and pairing ﬂuctuations.

FIG. 5. Two-, three- and four-hole binding energies as func- tions of U for (a) 3 × 4 and (b) 4 × 4 cylinders at quarter ﬁlling. The negative values of EB2 demonstrate robust two-hole pair- ing throughout the attractive regime. The sign change of EB3 at strong attractive interaction indicates ﬁnite-size-dependent three-hole clustering, while the positive values of EB4 show that stable four-hole bound states do not form within the parameter range studied.
